newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.KOREA'S JULY M2 MONEY SUPPLY UP 17.9 PCT YR/YR.
newsitem.headline: S.KOREA'S JULY M2 MONEY SUPPLY UP 17.9 PCT YR/YR.

text.p: South Korea's M2 money supply rose 17.9 percent in July year-on-year, against a 17.1 percent rise a year earlier, the central Bank of Korea (BOK) said on Thursday.
NOTE: M2 consists of money in circulation, checking account and savings account deposits with banks. MCT consists of M2, certificates of deposit (CD) and money in trust accounts.
A BOK official attributed the M2 rise to the shrinking current account deficit in July compared with a year earlier, and rising overseas borrowings with longer-term maturities by domestic companies.
A central bank statement showed about 390 billion won flowed in from those sectors in July. The bank is due to release the current account figures in the fourth week of this month.
But M2 growth showed signs of slowing down since May on falling corporate money demand due to the sluggish economy.
The official said the central bank would limit the M2 rise to about the 18 percent level in August.
The statement said private sector loans fell to 7.2 trillion won at the end of July from 10.81 trillion won a year earlier.
Bank loans to small- and medium-sized companies rose to 5.93 trillion won for the first 20 days of July against 4.58 trillion in the same period of 1996.

But credits granted by merchant banks fell sharply to 477.2 billion won during the period from 220.9 billion won a year ago after the financial crisis in the nation's eighth-largest Kia Group surfaced in July.
The government siphoned off 1.11 trillion won from money in circulation in July, compared to 4.81 trillion a year ago.
Direct financing by South Korean companies in local stock and bond markets in June increased to 650 billion won from 520 billion a year earlier, the statement said.
The statement said domestic companies raised their rights issue offers as May's expansion of the foreign stock ownership gave a boost to the local stock market.

Corporate bond issues in July totalled 930 billion won, compared with 607 billion a year ago. Yields on three-year bench market corporate bonds rose 11.86 percent in July against 11.65 percent a month ago.
